issues.title: [ROADMAP] Deep Native Engine AI learning ecosystem roadmap and delivery gates
ac: All 25 original CTP IDs and source provenance are retained. The current product direction supersedes contractor-only audience/admission assumptions, with explicit mapping to revised acceptance criteria.
Six phase epics and eight delivery milestones distinguish definition, first slice, full private MVP, verification, pilot, continuation, repeatability and expansion.
Every execution issue records acceptance criteria, non-goals, dependencies, accountable role, verification evidence and definition of done.
The user-confirmed 99% unit / 99% E2E journey coverage / 100% critical journey and required test-pass gates are explicit and consistent.

Current authorization covers planning, product-direction refactoring and repository setup, including verified merge to main. Application implementation, live integration verification and commercial activity retain their separate authorization gates.

Shared foundations, goal-based learning, bounded participation and reviewed contributions serve IT, non-IT professional and general learners in the private MVP. Contractor/career paths and paid coaching are optional.
issues.evidence: Published issue inventory, dependency audit, local source-copy checksums, milestone listing and planning-only git status.
issues.non_goals: This tracking issue is not authorization to implement, spend, publish a live product, contact prospects or collect payments. The planning deliverable can be complete while roadmap execution remains open.
issues.extra: MASTER

issues.title: [GATE-A] Phase A — Define and demonstrate
ac: Offer scope, private prototype, common foundation, assessment method, rights and capacity are reviewable. Missing real-world decisions are explicit launch blockers; no unavailable expertise is advertised.
All mandatory child AC/DoD outcomes are evidenced, with linked defects and explicit stop decisions; deferred options are recorded as such.
Owner records a dated stage decision; technical completion, production verification and commercial validation remain separate.
Approve the cross-audience story map, common learning/participation scope, access model and contribution/moderation rules under PRODUCT-DIRECTION.md. Contractor-only admission is superseded.
issues.evidence: Linked child evidence, stage review and explicit owner go/no-go/defer decision.
issues.non_goals: Indicative timing is not a promise. Current permission covers planning and repository setup; application implementation remains on hold.
issues.extra: Weeks 1-2 (relative estimate)

issues.title: [GATE-B] Phase B — Complete and verify the private MVP
ac: First complete member-review journey, then every required member/coach/operator flow, then full verification. Deterministic AI/payment/manual-provider flows work honestly. >=99% each unit metric; >=99% E2E scenario coverage; 100% critical coverage and required test passes. All full-MVP AC and release evidence pass.
All mandatory child AC/DoD outcomes are evidenced, with linked defects and explicit stop decisions; deferred options are recorded as such.
Owner records a dated stage decision; technical completion, production verification and commercial validation remain separate.

Full MVP includes ECO-01 through ECO-08: nontechnical/exploratory onboarding, suitable practical learning, opt-in learning circles and reviewed contributions, with optional coaching kept separate from common membership.
issues.evidence: Linked child evidence, stage review and explicit owner go/no-go/defer decision.

ac: Actual launch prerequisites and authorization precede real service. Five paid members across multiple roles, at least four useful reviewed completions, obligations fulfilled and measured delivery cost. Paid continuation is evaluated in Phase D.
All mandatory child AC/DoD outcomes are evidenced, with linked defects and explicit stop decisions; deferred options are recorded as such.
Owner records a dated stage decision; technical completion, production verification and commercial validation remain separate.

This gate validates the optional coached service, not eligibility for the broader ecosystem. Record background/goal coverage and learning outcomes without implying all audiences must buy the original pilot.

ac: At least three actual paid continuations plus useful recurring service and reviewed delivery economics. Failed thresholds trigger redesign/stop. A five-member sample remains directional.

ac: Each candidate expansion has an evidence-backed proceed/defer/decline decision. Only selected expansions need delivery proof; deferred options are not required to ship. No earlier gate implies approval for a new tier, country, integration or business model.

issues.title: [PLAN-001] Reconcile source context, scope, story map and open decisions
ac: The current PRODUCT-DIRECTION.md and revised live issues supersede contractor-only scope in the September 15 package; the original files and SHA-256 manifest remain unchanged.

Define the shared AI learning and participation ecosystem for IT practitioners, professionals in other fields, students/career changers, creators/entrepreneurs and curious learners. Backgrounds and goals may overlap; the nine IT families and contractor/career services are optional specializations.
Record owner, due decision, evidence and downstream blocker for entity, province/countries, budget, founder availability, providers, rights, experts and terms; unknowns are not guessed.
Produce a reviewable member/coach/operator story map and low-fidelity private prototype; distinguish first vertical slice from full Phase B.
Resolve source differences explicitly: preserve all nine roadmap journeys plus build-prompt usability/recovery, late-return and commercial-truth criteria.

Document foundation/participation access and pricing decisions separately from optional coaching hypotheses; do not assume a free tier or apply archived high-touch prices to every learner. Record which archived audience assumptions are superseded and preserve applicable commercial invariants.
issues.evidence: Source comparison, decision log, story-map/prototype review and scope sign-off.
issues.non_goals: No application implementation, live offer launch or fabricated demand. Preserve historical source and explicitly supersede contractor-only positioning with the current cross-audience learning ecosystem.

issues.title: [GOV-001] Adopt the AI-assisted development working agreement
ac: AGENTS.md and contribution/issue/PR guidance encode context-first, issue-first, bounded changes, behavior-first tests, diff review and durable decision/validation notes.
Definition of ready requires AC, dependencies, accountable owner, risk boundaries and test plan; backlog existence does not authorize coding.
Definition of done requires evidence on the intended revision, all AC, review, successful prescribed pre-push checks and CI, and relevant operational documentation.
Generated code and dependencies require independent review; current official APIs, licenses, lockfiles and secret/privacy boundaries are checked.
No automatic coding-agent assignment, test/coverage bypass, invented live results, or unrelated refactors; no remote actions outside actual authorization.
issues.evidence: Review of working agreement and issue/PR examples against this roadmap; repository guidance is unambiguous about the current planning-only boundary.
issues.non_goals: Do not implement workflows, install tools or change repository protections in this planning issue.
issues.extra: References: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/responsible-use/agents and https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices . These support review and behavioral testing; the 99% target is the user requirement.

issues.title: [PLAN-002] Prepare entity, jurisdiction, terms, privacy and payment launch decisions
ac: Record actual operating entity/province, enabled customer countries, decision owners and qualified advice needed before launch; unresolved items visibly block live sales.
Review offer/cancellation/refund/renewal language, invoice and tax classification, training classification, privacy/retention, AI vendors, insurance and IP permissions for the actual jurisdiction.
Separate learning, AI processing, recording, portfolio and marketing consent; define retention exceptions and accurate deletion statements.
Prepare an owner-reviewed launch decision checklist and evidence locations without asserting legal clearance from a draft or from software tests.

Define member-contribution attribution/rights, opt-in public or group visibility, community rules, reporting/moderation responsibilities and consent boundaries for the actual supported audiences before public participation.
issues.evidence: Dated decision register, reviewed draft terms/policies, adviser/owner determinations and unresolved launch blockers.
issues.non_goals: No signing, tax/legal conclusions from generic guidance, purchases, card charges or publication.

issues.title: [PLAN-003] Reserve qualified expert capacity and define service operations
ac: Roster records verifiable expertise, role/domain, service types, availability, loaded cost, conflicts and backup; distinguish proposed contacts from actual commitments.
Model pilot two 60-minute coaching units, four 30-minute review units and two monthly 60-minute support allocations, plus internal onboarding reserve of 60 coach/30 support minutes.
Plan four one-hour pooled clinics per month with at most 16 members per group; count preparation, notes, QA, scheduling slack and support once.
Publish proposed scope/turnaround/24-hour cancellation/no-show/service-recovery rules and staffed hours separately from final accepted terms.

Confirm capacity before promising tailored paid coaching or formal expert review. Missing specialized coverage must be visible without excluding people from the common learning/participation path or requiring everyone to buy coaching.
issues.evidence: Capacity workbook/roster, example cohort allocation, expert evidence and owner-reviewed operating procedures.
issues.non_goals: No invented expert credentials, hiring commitments, unlimited service or customer admission.

issues.title: [PLAN-004] Prepare the common foundation and reviewed demonstration content pack
ac: Specify six accessible foundation lessons covering AI literacy, useful prompting, checking outputs, privacy/rights, practical workflows and collaborative participation. Include beginner, IT and non-IT exercise paths, with no mandatory coding or employment prerequisite.

Prepare at least two complete synthetic reference assignments spanning a technical path (such as QA) and a nontechnical professional/general-learner path (such as meeting-action planning), with versioned rubrics and reviewer calibration.
Prepare three maintained workflow demonstrations: requirements-to-acceptance drafting, test-case review and meeting-action extraction.

Every asset has owner, sources/rights, version, limitations, intended goals/backgrounds, prerequisites, review date and readiness; generated examples remain demonstrations until reviewed for their intended use.
Exercises and formal reviews fit their actual scope and funded allocation; noncoding learners receive a complete suitable path and formal expert assessment is distinct from peer/AI feedback.

Prepare examples of learner questions, peer responses and a reviewed contribution with attribution. Distinguish community participation from qualified assessment and verify plain-language and accessibility requirements.
issues.evidence: Content inventory, sample lessons/assignments/reference outputs, rights checks, calibration notes and qualified sign-off where available.
issues.non_goals: No claims of expert approval, accreditation or paid curriculum readiness without evidence.

issues.title: [QA-001] Establish meaningful unit coverage gates at 99%
ac: Choose and document the maintained runner/instrumentation and cover all first-party executable app source, including unimported files.
Enforce >=99% independently for lines, branches, statements and functions globally and per logical module; record raw counts, scope and reviewed exclusions.
Only justified generated/vendor/non-executable artifacts may be excluded; missing reports, no tests and zero denominators fail.
Behavioral cases exercise money/date/permission/state/validation errors; targeted mutation or fault injection demonstrates assertions detect broken critical rules.
Intentionally lower coverage on a throwaway fixture to demonstrate the gate fails, restore it, and record a successful meaningful baseline.
issues.evidence: Runner config, inclusion/exclusion review, machine-readable report and failure/success gate demonstration on an identified revision.
issues.non_goals: No coverage padding, mocked-away business rules, threshold reductions or claimed current 99% result.
issues.extra: Coverage guidance: https://vitest.dev/config/coverage.html . Tool choice remains an implementation decision.

issues.title: [QA-002] Build E2E scenario traceability and the 99% journey coverage gate
ac: Version a scenario register mapping each source journey and issue AC to actor, preconditions, steps, observable results, risk and browser test IDs.

Coverage = distinct passing automated in-scope scenario IDs / all approved in-scope scenario IDs; >=99% is mandatory. Pending, missing, failed, skipped, quarantined or retry-only scenarios remain uncovered.
Critical isolation, payments/dates, consent, ledgers/races, AI failures/budgets, deletion and the complete member-review journey require 100% coverage; all required executed tests pass.
Keep first-slice and full-MVP scopes explicit; the full-release denominator includes unimplemented scenarios. Denominator changes require reviewed scope decisions, never silent removal.
Run real UI/server/database with independent synthetic contexts and external-only deterministic adapters; use observable outcomes and resilient accessible locators.
Demonstrate gate failure for missing mapping, skipped critical case, empty report and failing test; preserve traces and first-attempt failure information.

Add ECO-01 through ECO-08 from ECOSYSTEM-JOURNEYS.md, mapping IT, non-IT and general learners to applicable AC. Preserve original cases and record reviewed overlap/scope changes; broader audiences cannot be used to remove difficult commercial/privacy tests.
issues.evidence: Versioned journey register, scenario-to-test map, reproducible runner, denominator report and deliberate failure checks.
issues.non_goals: Do not equate test count, test pass rate, UI code coverage or mocked pages with journey coverage.
issues.extra: The user explicitly selected journey coverage rather than browser-instrumented code coverage. Reference: https://playwright.dev/docs/best-practices .

issues.title: [QA-003] Enforce full verification before every push and required CI checks
ac: Provide one documented local command for formatting/lint, type checks, unit coverage, integration tests, applicable full E2E matrix, production build and relevant security checks.
Pre-push execution fails closed on test/report/coverage failure and records exact intended tree or revision, environment, commands and report locations; changed code invalidates prior evidence.
Document and exercise a verified bootstrap path while the harness is introduced; no application change is pushed without executable verification.
CI independently repeats gates on the PR/merge candidate; install required-check settings only after observed workflow jobs exist and have run.

Demonstrate a failing push gate locally without sending a failing revision; demonstrate successful checks before a permitted push. No --no-verify, skipped assertions, hidden retries or reduced targets.
Record reviewer approval and resolve blocking findings before merge; checks unavailable due to infrastructure remain blocked rather than waived silently.
issues.evidence: Pre-push failure/success evidence, exact-revision local reports, CI URLs and verified required-job names once implementation is authorized.
issues.non_goals: No hook or Actions code, protection changes, commit, push or merge during the current planning session.

issues.title: [QA-004] Define the threat model, data boundaries and risk-based test matrix
ac: Map trust boundaries for workspaces, staff grants, object storage, uploads, AI retrieval, jobs, payments, secrets and operator access.
Specify negative cases for cross-record ownership, privilege escalation, expiring/revoked links, unsafe files, prompt injection, consent bypass, leaked logs and unauthorized exports.
Specify transaction, idempotency, timeout/retry and date invariants with reproduction plans; connect them to CTP-023 and every affected feature.
Define dependency/secret/security scan policy, threat owners, response procedure and release-blocking severity; no unsupported security certification claims.

Threat-model cohort membership, moderator permissions, learner-contribution publication, reports and removal/revocation. Treat member-provided content as untrusted; joining a group never implicitly shares private work or permits unsolicited outreach.
issues.evidence: Reviewed data-flow/threat model, abuse-case register and issue/test mapping with owners.
issues.non_goals: No security code or production security settings changed yet.

issues.title: [QA-005] Verify accessibility, browser compatibility and performance budgets
ac: Core member/coach/operator journeys work at mobile and desktop widths, keyboard-only navigation, readable labels/focus/errors and page-reload recovery.
Run the approved Chromium/Firefox/WebKit matrix with deterministic data; automate meaningful accessibility checks and perform manual keyboard/focus review.
Approve quantitative response-time, concurrency, upload-size and background-job budgets based on the five-member pilot and operator workloads before measuring.
Record test environment, data volume, p50/p95 timings, failures and accessibility defects; agreed budgets and critical usability criteria pass before release.
Verify the common learning and participation journeys with noncoding/beginner language, accessible contribution/group controls and the same browser/keyboard expectations as technical paths.
issues.evidence: Browser matrix reports/traces, keyboard/accessibility review and measured workload results compared with approved budgets.
issues.non_goals: No arbitrary performance promise, screenshot-only acceptance or universal accessibility certification.

issues.title: [CTP-001] Audit project and record architecture decisions
ac: Read project instructions; inventory reusable auth, design, billing, tests, and owned content; record reuse/greenfield decision and exact tools chosen from current official docs.
No unrelated repository changes.

Record the current planning/tooling-only checkout and its product direction without resurrecting removed historical code. Decide app placement, modular monolith boundaries, relational schema/migrations, storage/jobs and maintained packages in an ADR.

Separate learner goals/backgrounds, curated tracks, participation/contributions, optional offers and privileged staff authorization in the domain model; legacy Professional pricing or contractor fields cannot define the universal member identity.
issues.evidence: Repository inventory, architecture/data-flow ADRs, official-doc references and first-slice test plan.
issues.non_goals: No copying other projects or choosing a stack solely from the old repository description.
issues.extra: Original source: finalized 03-roadmap-and-backlog.md, CTP-001. Full source acceptance criteria are retained above; supplements preserve detail from the final build prompt.

issues.title: [CTP-002] Define learning access and optional coaching offers
ac: Represent shared learning/participation access separately from optional coaching offers. The archived Professional/Specialist/Practice/Partner prices and service quotas are coaching-offer hypotheses, not universal membership requirements.
Pilot grants two 60-minute coaching units and four 30-minute review units across two billing periods, plus stated support/AI.
CAD 3,000→CAD 9,000→CAD 12,000 phases preserve anniversary.
Only explicitly approved live offers are purchasable. Separate foundational access rules from coaching purchase; background tags such as professional do not assign a paid plan or staff privileges.

Use integer CAD cents and immutable offer/terms versions. Professional monthly service is 60 coach/30 review/30 support minutes; pilot support is 60 minutes per billing month; preserve internal onboarding reserve separately. No annual prepayment releases all future monthly credits.

Foundation/participation access must have explicit approved rules and limits independent of coaching acceptance. Mark unsettled commercial choices as pending; never silently grant unbudgeted services or invent a new price/free tier.
issues.evidence: Table-driven offer, price, quota and historical-version tests plus UI/server agreement comparison.
issues.non_goals: No live checkout or unauthorized higher-tier sale.
issues.extra: Original source: finalized 03-roadmap-and-backlog.md, CTP-002. Full source acceptance criteria are retained above; supplements preserve detail from the final build prompt.

issues.title: [CTP-003] Implement learner backgrounds, goals, track readiness and expert registry
ac: Support IT practitioners, non-IT professionals and general/exploratory learners with optional multi-background/domain tags, experience and goals. The nine IT role families remain optional technical subcategories; no job, client or contractor status is required.
Available/limited coverage/in preparation/retired states display accurately.
Expert role/domain, service types, dates, costs, and backup coverage are recorded.
No unsupported tailored service can be committed.

Members can choose or revise a primary learning goal and an exploratory path. General learners can enter the common foundation; manual fit/capacity review applies to specialized services, not blanket admission. Track readiness reflects reviewed content and real qualified coverage where promised.
issues.evidence: Background/goal/track-readiness transition tests for IT, non-IT professional and exploratory learners; unsupported tailored-service states without blanket admission refusal.
issues.non_goals: No claim of full domain expertise from broad intake.

issues.title: [CTP-004] Create deterministic adapters and configuration validation
ac: Synthetic seeds cover distinct IT, non-IT professional and general-learner accounts; multiple goals; paid and non-coaching membership states; an assigned/revoked coach, reviewer, editor, moderator and operator.
AI/payment/storage/calendar/email adapters separate demo/test/live modes.
Missing live settings produce actionable disabled states; no fake sent message or live payment confirmation.

Isolate test/live databases, buckets and credentials; validate auth and analytics adapters too. Demo impersonation cannot run live. Failed jobs survive reload with sanitized errors and bounded retries.
issues.evidence: Adapter contract tests and missing-configuration/demo-to-live isolation checks.
issues.non_goals: No paid services, real messages or production credentials required for the private MVP.

issues.title: [CTP-005] Implement identity, workspace authorization, and staff grants
ac: Members own private workspaces.
Coach/reviewer access is assignment-scoped and time-bounded; editor role grants no member-data access.
Direct API requests cannot bypass boundaries; revocation prevents new access; privileged support access is logged.
Server derives identity/workspace; members cannot self-grant staff roles. Cross-record references cannot join another workspace. Support content access has purpose, expiry and an audit trail.
Learner background/goal changes do not grant coach/reviewer/editor/moderator privileges; cohort membership grants only its explicitly permitted shared content.
issues.evidence: Role/record authorization matrix, expiry/revocation integration cases and adversarial direct-API tests.
issues.non_goals: No client-only authorization or global staff access.
issues.extra: Original source: finalized 03-roadmap-and-backlog.md, CTP-005. Full source acceptance criteria are retained above; supplements preserve detail from the final build prompt.

issues.title: [CTP-006] Implement evidence consent, private upload, and quarantine
ac: Allowlisted size/type rules, malware/quarantine state, sharing permission, and private object storage work.
Invalid objects cannot reach review.
Every download rechecks authorization; short-lived links, metadata/log redaction, and deletion hooks are verified.
Require explicit rights/sharing scope, never execute uploads, and cover rejected types, quarantine transitions, revoked grants and derived-data deletion. Logs contain no raw evidence.
Separate permission to submit privately for review from permission to publish a community contribution or share with a learning circle; each destination requires explicit scope.
issues.evidence: Storage policy tests and browser upload/download/rejection/revocation cases with independent members.
issues.non_goals: No public storage bucket or unrestricted client-document intake.

issues.title: [CTP-007] Implement versioned content, sources, rubrics, and publication
ac: Draft/preview/review/publish/retire workflow is real.
Each available item has owner, sources/rights, review date, supported goals/backgrounds/domain, prerequisites and version.
Assessments pin rubric/content versions; new releases do not rewrite earlier results.

Search/filter and accessible previews use eligible published versions. Support the shared six-lesson foundation and cross-audience exercises from PLAN-004; distinguish curated instruction, proposed member contributions and qualified formal assessment.
issues.evidence: Publication/retirement/rights/version-pinning tests and editor/member browser evidence.
issues.non_goals: No fake reviewer sign-off or retroactive assessment rewrite.

issues.title: [CTP-008] Implement learner onboarding, goal-based plans and optional offers
ac: People across IT, other professions and general learning interests can join the common foundation without a job title, client, contract, coding experience or purchase of the Professional coaching offer.
Present foundation/participation access conditions separately from optional paid services; a member sees actual covered scope, price and confirmed capacity before any paid acceptance.
Self-reported experience remains labelled.

An initial learning plan fits the member goals, experience and available time. Exploratory/noncoding paths are valid; optional 90-day coaching plans fit funded services and never fabricate credentials.
Capture timezone/goals/weekly availability and separate consent choices; sensitive income/client/contract dates stay optional. Require real qualified capacity before accepting tailored paid scope.
issues.evidence: Browser onboarding for IT, non-IT professional and general learners without mandatory contractor/coding/coaching-purchase fields; optional covered-offer acceptance and declined-specialized-service tests.
issues.non_goals: No identity documents or client credentials in normal onboarding.

issues.title: [CTP-009] Implement lesson reader, progress, and assignment selection
ac: A member reads actual accessible material/transcript, completes an exercise, and sees accurate next actions.
Choose assignments by learning goal, experience, interests and actual prerequisites; include complete noncoding and exploratory paths.
Progress reflects observed activity/completion, never synthetic earnings or hiring outcomes.
Lesson/transcript and progress survive reload; useful empty/error states and next actions work after a goal change. Role or employment labels do not force a generic coding assessment.
issues.evidence: Reader/progress/assignment browser traces with reload and error recovery.
issues.non_goals: No completion flag treated as verified competence.

issues.title: [CTP-010] Implement submission versions, human review, and revisions
ac: Qualified assigned reviewer sees only the authorized version, records criterion-level feedback with evidence references and time spent, and publishes a review.
Revision creates new evidence; prior feedback remains intact.
Simulated assignments stay labelled in any portfolio output.

Only the assigned human can publish formal assessment; distinguish AI suggestions/self-report/human review. Include bounded clarification/appeal. Account for prep/time, then reconcile funded review consumption with CTP-011 before full-MVP closure.

Offer goal-appropriate evidence and revisions across technical and nontechnical paths. Peer/AI feedback is labelled and cannot publish formal assessment or consume expert service credits as if delivered by a qualified reviewer.
issues.evidence: Submission/rubric immutability, reviewer authorization, revision/appeal and time/entitlement integration evidence.
issues.non_goals: No unlimited revisions or AI-only formal assessment.

issues.title: [CTP-011] Implement immutable entitlement reservations and ledger
ac: Grant/reserve/consume/release/expire/adjust events use idempotency keys and immutable history.
Atomic checks prevent overspending.
Whole-minute human budgets include preparation; separate categories never silently substitute.
Pilot/continuation/month-end grants reconcile without a duplicate annual bundle.

Test integer-minute/category invariants, membership-anchored months, leap years, Jan-31 and expiry. Pilot plus continuation yields 12 bookable coach hours and 7 review hours in year one; onboarding capacity is separate. Integrate review/support/AI settlements exactly once.
Model learning/participation access separately from optional paid service-minute and AI budgets; joining a cohort or changing professional background never mints paid-service grants.
issues.evidence: Transactional/property-based ledger tests, last-unit races and full annual reconciliation fixture.
issues.non_goals: No mutable historical ledger, category substitution or duplicate annual bundles.

issues.title: [CTP-012] Implement expert capacity, booking, and policy exceptions
ac: Local timezone availability shows qualified slots.
Concurrent booking has one winner; booking reserves service and capacity atomically.
The 24-hour proposed window/no-show/provider-cancel policies behave as disclosed.
Provider-caused failure issues a dated replacement credit and logs both histories.
Expire holds safely; distinguish allowance from qualified availability. Test DST/timezones, 45-call-plus-15-prep coach allocation and staff rescheduling. No unconfigured email/calendar success claim.
Capacity admission applies to a promised expert service, not ordinary membership or peer learning. Present unavailable specialized coverage without blocking the shared foundation.
issues.evidence: Real-database last-slot/last-credit races and browser booking/cancellation/recovery cases.
issues.non_goals: No overselling capacity or silent service-credit loss.

issues.title: [CTP-013] Implement maintained workflow registry and downloads
ac: Published bundles have setup, synthetic inputs, expected outputs, tests, permission/cost limits, version compatibility, license, owner, and last verification.
Retired/stale versions warn accurately.
Downloading does not execute code or connect to a client system.
Seed the three specified synthetic workflows, with copy/download and private feedback. Demonstrate supported examples without connecting member/client systems.

Include goal/prerequisite tags and approachable nontechnical workflows. Members can propose attributed improvements through the reviewed contribution lifecycle; downloading or sharing a proposal never executes it.
issues.evidence: Bundle completeness/license review, declared-environment example verification and download UI test.
issues.non_goals: No server-side arbitrary code execution or automatic external actions.

issues.title: [CTP-014] Implement AI gateway, consent, token/cost budgets, and jobs
ac: No sharing consent means no dispatch of private evidence.
Approved models, input limits, queue/concurrency, idempotency, cost reservation/reconciliation, and kill switch work.
Timeout ambiguity is reconciled before costly retry.
Estimated cost is labelled; platform failures restore allowances.

Treat evidence/retrieval as untrusted data; validate output schema and ownership. Persist job state, provider IDs and prompt/model versions without raw private telemetry. Handle ambiguous timeouts before redispatch.

Apply consent and budget checks equally across learner paths; community posts and contributed resources are untrusted context, not instructions that can override provider permissions or private-data boundaries.
issues.evidence: Consent/queue/idempotency/budget-kill/failure-restoration tests and provider contract fault injection.
